2  ORDER (Order of the Court was made by the Hon'ble Chief Justice)

At the outset, petitioner seeks leave to delete respondents 4 and 5.
Leave granted.

Registry to delete respondents 4 and 5.
2.

In this petition, petitioner is seeking a declaration to declare Act 33 of 1986 and Act 31 of 2003 of the Tamil Nadu Prohibition Act, 1937 as immoral, unconstitutional, against right to life and hence,
illegal.
3.
Both these Acts have been in force for the last 38 and 21 years respectively.
Therefore, we are not inclined to entertain the petition.
The writ petition is dismissed.

4. At the same time, in the order dated 29.07.2024, petitioner was permitted to submit a fresh representation to the Government because whether to lift a ban on toddy is a policy decision that the Government has to take.
_ https://www.mhc.tn.gov.in/judis 5.
Petitioner states that he has not filed any representation.
If petitioner files any representation within four weeks, representation be considered and if necessary, petitioner be called to make a presentation.

Learned Additional Advocate General states that the representation be made to Principal Secretary,
Prohibition and Excise Department.
6. The writ petition is dismissed.
There shall be no order as to costs.
Consequently, the interim applications also stand dismissed.
(K.R.SHRIRAM, CJ) (SENTHILKUMAR RAMAMOORTHY  24.01.2025  Index : Yes/No
